printbridge_meta: Learn how the optional Print Bridge utility connects SSCC Labels to a ZPL-compatible network printer on your local network.
printbridge_heading: Print labels directly to your network printer
printbridge_intro: Print Bridge is a separate, open-source utility that runs on your computer and optionally connects SSCC Labels to a ZPL-compatible network printer. You can continue to download PDF and ZPL files without installing it. Browsers can't send print jobs directly to a local printer, so Print Bridge acts as a small, local go-between.
printbridge_step1_desc: Create and save a label in SSCC Labels. Printing uses that saved label and its existing SSCC.
printbridge_step2_desc: Choose Print via bridge. The browser sends the label's print data to Print Bridge running on your computer.
printbridge_step3_desc: Print Bridge forwards the ZPL to the network printer you configured. The hosted web app does not connect to your local network.
printbridge_need1: Print Bridge installed and running on the same computer as your browser.
printbridge_need2: A ZPL-compatible network printer reachable from that computer.
printbridge_need3: Your printer address, port, and resolution configured in SSCC Labels under Settings → Printer.
printbridge_setup_desc: The setup instructions and installer downloads are maintained in the Print Bridge
printbridge_screenshot_caption: Print Bridge running on your computer, forwarding ZPL to your printer.
printbridge_need_this_body: If you only download PDF or ZPL files, you don't need it. Install it only if you want one-click printing to a ZPL printer.
printbridge_faq_safe_a: Print Bridge is open source and only connects to the printer you configure. The hosted web app never touches your local network.
printbridge_faq_offline_a: Print Bridge runs on your computer and works on your local network. You still need an internet connection to open SSCC Labels and load saved labels.
printbridge_faq_printers_a: Any ZPL-compatible network printer reachable from the computer running Print Bridge.

guide_custom_request_success: Your request was sent. We will reply by email.
guide_intro2: The free generator supports three label workflows. Compare their static label samples, then follow the steps from company setup to saving a real label.
guide_setup_company: Set up your company before creating a real SSCC
guide_setup_desc: Every real logistic label needs an SSCC. Creating one requires a GS1 Company Prefix licensed to your organization; the app cannot create a valid SSCC without it. You can inspect the examples below without signing in. These static samples follow the app's single-label print layouts and use the sample data shown in Figure 4-1 of the GS1 Logistic Label Guideline.
guide_company_name_desc: saved in your profile and used on labels where appropriate.
guide_gs1_prefix_desc: your organization's licensed prefix is required to allocate a real SSCC and is not printed as a separate field on these samples.
guide_ext_serial_label: Extension digit and next serial reference:
guide_ext_serial_desc: used with your prefix to allocate an SSCC when you save a label.
guide_ship_same_desc: Save your products with their GTINs in Settings, then select one when creating an identical-contents label to fill its GTIN. Shipment details such as lot, date, count, and addresses stay on each label.
guide_download_print_desc: All three supported label workflows are available as PDF and ZPL. Downloads keep the saved label's layout, information, and SSCC, so downloading another format does not create a new SSCC.
guide_pdf_desc2: A PDF downloads automatically when you generate and save a label. You can download it again from Saved labels. Print at 100% scale on matching label stock to preserve barcode dimensions.
guide_zpl_step1: Generate and save your label, or use an existing record in Saved labels.
guide_zpl_step2: Set ZPL printer resolution to match your printer: 203, 300, or 600 dpi. Check your printer settings if you are unsure.
guide_zpl_step3: Click Download ZPL, then send the downloaded .zpl file using your printer software.
guide_zpl_media: Use media and a printer wide enough for the selected layout. A 6 × 8 label requires a six-inch print width. The two-copy layout places both copies on one 4 × 6 sheet.
guide_test_bridge: Test bridge connection checks that the bridge is reachable; check your first physical label too.
guide_beyond_free: Need something beyond the free generator?
guide_beyond_free_desc: The three free workflows cover common logistic-label needs. If a customer requirement needs a different layout, printer workflow, or integration, we can discuss a tailored project.
guide_possible_starting: Possible starting points include customer routing-guide fields, other label sizes or print formats, printer delivery, shipment data, user roles, and integrations. Each request is reviewed individually.
guide_suggest_improvement: Suggest an improvement or discuss a project
guide_custom_request_desc2: Choose whether you are suggesting an improvement to the free tool or asking about a specific project. No account is needed. Your message and reply address will be sent by email and will not be saved in the application.
